speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) how much fail-safe redundancy is designed into (i) Singapore's domestic broadband Internet networks and (ii) offshore Internet connectivity; and (b) whether there are plans to enhance system redundancy in light of the growing dependency on Internet access which will arise from the Smart Nation initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: He has raised an issue that is important to both my Ministry and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA), which is the resilience of our international and domestic Internet connectivity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The fact that we had sufficient diversity and redundancy in international Internet connectivity enabled us to reroute traffic through undamaged cables.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: In contrast, Internet connections in a number of countries in the Asia Pacific were disrupted.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Broadband Internet services are offered by multiple operators over multiple networks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: These include the Nationwide Broadband Network, mobile networks and operators' own fixed-line networks.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This diversity reduces the risks due to reliance on a single set of infrastructure and makes our domestic broadband Internet connectivity more resilient.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: My Ministry and IMDA regularly review and put in place measures to enhance the resilience of our broadband Internet services.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It aims to ensure that operators of key telecommunication infrastructure invest in and enhance the resilience of their networks against service disruptions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: Other measures include IMDA's requirements for key fixed and mobile operators to conduct regular audits on their network designs, operational processes, business continuity planning and associated infrastructure and facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We will work closely with the industry to ensure that these regulations remain appropriate, effective and up to date.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: This is all the more critical as we strive to become a Smart Nation and Digital Economy.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: We will continuously monitor and review our policies and regulations to achieve this goal.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Does our current planning consider potential major natural disasters, besides typhoons, for example?

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In fact, we have learnt from the previous incidents so that we can enhance the resilience of our network.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: In other words, we learn, study and see where the points of systemic risks are and how we can overcome them.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: On the Member's second question as to whether or not we conduct table-top exercises, what IMDA does is they work with the operators to ensure that, first, their own network must be resilient; and, secondly, the overall connectivity, and the possible systemic effects of one network over the other are also addressed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: So, we have to make sure that connectivity remains resilient.
